findings.title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. This is a copy-paste error: `rawTokenId` is never null-checked, so a null `rawTokenId` will pass construction and cause a NullPointerException later (e.g., in `encodeTokenId` when concatenating).

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices
findings.body: Two bugs in `isAccessTokenId`: (1) The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted—it returns false when the shortcut matches instead of when it doesn't match (missing `!`). (2) The substring indices are wrong: in the 6-char prefix (e.g., `onrtac`), the grant type occupies indices 4–5, but the code extracts `substring(3, 5)` which gives characters at indices 3–4 (e.g., `ta` from `onrtac`). The correct call is `substring(4, 6)`. Combined, the matcher almost always returns true regardless of the actual grant type, making the test assertions ineffective.

findings.title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking change
findings.body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Although this is in `server-spi-private`, any extension or internal code that was constructing a `Context` from an existing `Context` instance will fail to compile after this change. If this constructor was used anywhere in the codebase or by known extensions, this is a source-incompatible change that should be documented or deprecated first.

findings.title: Duplicate shortcut validation does not detect all collision scenarios
findings.body: The check `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` only detects collisions when two grants share the same shortcut (shrinking grantsByShortcuts) or two shortcuts map to the same grant name (shrinking grantsToShortcuts). If two grants have the same shortcut AND the same ID (unlikely but possible with misconfiguration), both maps would have the same size and the collision would go undetected. A more robust approach would be to check that the number of entries inserted equals the number of grant factories iterated.
